newsitem.title: UK: UK cancels tax credits for share buybacks.
newsitem.headline: UK cancels tax credits for share buybacks.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Tuesday that shareholders who previously would have been able to claim tax credits on share buyacks or special dividend payouts will no longer be able to do so, effective today.
Clarke said in a statement that the move stemmed from "...the growing loss of tax through schemes involving companies buying their own shares or paying special dividends..."
He said a provision would be included in the next Finance Bill to change the tax treatment of such schemes in certain circumstances, effective October 8.

"We have seen recently companies buying their own shares or paying special dividends in such a way that the proceeds end up almost entirely in the hands of those who are entitled to payment of a tax credit. This has costs for the Exchequer, and if action is not taken soon that cost would escalate," he said.
"The Inland Revenue will continue to monitor the situation, and we will not hesitate to take any necessary further action should further evidence of abuse appear," he added.
He said the new treatment would apply to the following distributions made on or after 8 October:
- redemption, repayment or purchase by a company of its own shares

- a distribution associated with transactions in shares or securities, including special dividends linked to share consolidations, and special dividends following a takeover where those dividends are effectively part of the bid.
He said that such distributions would be treated in the same way as foreign income dividends (FIDs) which means companies which make such distributions must account for advance corporation tax (ACT).
He said that these provisions would prevent shareholders from obtaining a tax advantage from various "artificial transactions in securities."
He added that the change would make it clear that a tax advantage could include obtaining a payable tax credit.
He said that under the proposed changes, the position of taxpayers would remain largely unaffected.

The new regime will not affect either the treatment of special dividends not linked to share consolidations, takeovers or other transactions in shares or securities or the purchase by a company of its own shares from dealers.
